name: al-Ahwas al-Ansari
bio: Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Ansari, of the clan of Dubay'a, was a poet of Medina and a contemporary of Jarir and al-Farazdaq; al-Zirikli calls him “a satirist, pure in style, of the rank of Jamil ibn Ma'mar and Nusayb”. He was nicknamed al-Ahwas for a narrowness at the outer corners of his eyes, and the transmitter Hammad al-Rawiya ranked him above the other poets of his day in love poetry. He visited the caliph al-Walid ibn Abd al-Malik in Syria and was honoured, but al-Walid later heard things about his conduct that displeased him, sent him back to Medina to be flogged, and exiled him to Dahlak, an island between Yemen and Abyssinia where the Umayyads sent those who angered them. He stayed there until after the death of Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, until Yazid ibn Abd al-Malik set him free; he went to Damascus and died there in 105 AH (723 CE).
